question: This is one agent utterance from a customer-service call in Mainland Mandarin. Does it contain English-shaped translationese or clearly unnatural word choice?
native_does: Pass natural spoken Mainland Mandarin, including ordinary service formality, colloquial phrasing, and established borrowings or code-switching that sound natural. Names, identifiers, codes, and product names may remain as given. An English interface, setting, or status label passes when the context establishes that it is the actual displayed label or it is naturally mirrored from the customer; do not assume that every generic English technical phrase is such a label. Ignore harmless transcription spacing or punctuation. Judge language use only, not listening accuracy, facts, policy compliance, or task success.
ai_likely_does: Inspect every complete clause and phrase independently. A clearly unnatural local collocation or selectional mismatch is a violation even when the rest of the utterance is fluent. Flag wording that would sound clearly odd to a Mainland Mandarin speaker because it follows English structure or idiom word for word; uses forced nominal or passive phrasing, unnatural pronouns, connectors, or aspect particles; uses an unnatural word choice, collocation, or literal coinage; inserts unnecessary English, especially a cluster of generic settings, permissions, or statuses where ordinary Chinese is expected; or exposes raw backend or system language as customer-facing speech. One clear instance is enough. Do not flag mere formality, a smoother alternative, or wording that is only slightly awkward. For interrupted turns, judge complete material before the cutoff and ignore only the clipped ending.
